title: Telemetry ingest trust layer and backpressure playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a defendable 'trust layer' inside the usage event ingestion path that enforces structural invariants, applies graceful backpressure, and produces deterministic auditable outcomes for downstream console analytics. This ticket covers design decisions, a phased implementation targeting the Concert ingestion cluster, integration tests, and an operational playbook for on-call to triage schema drift and ingestion pressure events.
acceptance_criteria: Trust layer validates top-level event envelope and rejects only when required fields are missing or malformed (strict mode) and tags events for soft-coercion when recoverable (per-field evidence)
Backpressure mechanism triggers at defined queue/latency thresholds and emits a throttling signal that clients can surface via 429 headers or retry hints for SDKs
Fallback routing to lightweight ingress adapter when full validation pipeline is degraded (<=99.9% of requests continue to flow)
End-to-end test harness simulates 10k RPS bursts with mixed well-formed and malformed payloads and shows latency and successful throughput targets are met
Operational playbook documented with runbook steps, dashboards, and automatic pager rules for repeated schema drift (>5% malformed rate over 5min)
Observability: per-tenant metrics for accepted/soft-coerced/rejected events and histogram of validation latency are exported to Grafana and OpenTelemetry backends
technical_notes: Introduce a lightweight pre-validate filter (Rust) to cheaply assert envelope integrity and route to full validator only when the event passes initial gating
Full validator runs in a horizontally autoscalable pool; use proto-based typed checks for core fields (timestamp, tenant_id, event_type) and declarative JSON schema rules for optional feature flags
Soft-coercion records original payload + coercion operations in an append-only S3 location partitioned by date and tenant, with a retention of 30 days for auditability

Backpressure is implemented with a token-bucket fed controller: when queue latency > 300ms or queue length > 5000, start rejecting low-priority telemetry with 429 and 'Retry-After' header; high-priority (billing, billing-actors) always allowed
Provide an API contract version header (X-Ingest-Version) so clients can be progressively rolled forward; validator supports a compatibility table for last 3 contract versions
Use canary rollout: 1% of traffic to trust layer v1 -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated metrics guardrails before each step
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge pre-validate filter and unit tests. Deploy to staging ingestion cluster and run synthetic workloads
Week 2: Deploy full validator in canary (1% traffic). Monitor rejection rate and latency metrics. Iterate on coercion rules for common malformed events
Week 3: Expand canary to 25% and enable soft-coercion logging to audit store. Run retention policy and verify downstream jobs consume audit logs
Week 4: Full production roll; enable backpressure thresholds. Coordinate with SDK team to surface 429 details and retry hints
Post-roll: Run a 72-hour soak with daily review and one rollback capability; document final playbook and training for on-call
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Patel: Initial ticket created after post-mortem of 2026-02-08 ingest surge. Goal is to reduce silent data loss by making validation outcomes observable and recoverable.
2026-02-16 Owen Ramirez: Proposal posted for pre-validate filter in RFC doc (drive: https://drive.company.com/r/ingest-trust-layer-rfc). Asking infra for queue metrics export into staging cluster.
2026-02-22 Design review: Agreed to keep coercion rules minimal for week 1 and rely on audit logs for later refinements. DES-118 will own UX for reporting coerced events in console

2026-03-01 QA: Synthetic load harness (github: https://github.com/redwood/ingest-load-harness/pull/29) validated 10k RPS with 0.8% soft-coercion and 0.03% hard rejections. Noted timeout spike on validator pod during GC—need smaller heap and more frequent compaction
2026-03-05 Infra: Autoscaler policy adjusted; validator pool min=6 max=120. Added node tainting to prefer isolated hosts for high-priority tenants
2026-03-10 Owen Ramirez: Canary at 5% for Concert cluster. Metrics look stable. Next step expand to 25% after confirming SDK retry behavior with client teams
